title: quercus appenina subsp. amplifolia
intro: Quercus appenina subsp. amplifolia, commonly known as the Dinaric white oak, is a subspecies of deciduous tree that belongs to the beech family, Fagaceae. This plant is known for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, making it a valuable resource for traditional medicine. The therapeutic actions of Quercus appenina subsp. amplifolia include wound healing, antiseptic, and antipyretic effects, while its bioactive constituents include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins, which contribute to its medicinal properties. However, further research is needed to fully understand the extent of its health benefits and therapeutic applications.
